Question B-002-003-005.

Why the correct answer is right: Use VHF and UHF for local contacts when suitable so HF spectrum remains less cluttered for longer-distance communication.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Because greater output power is permitted on VHF and UHF": The reason is not that VHF/UHF automatically allow more output power; it is about appropriate use of bands.
- sourceIndex 2: "Because HF transmissions are not propagated locally": HF can certainly support local paths in some conditions, so “not propagated locally” is too absolute.
- sourceIndex 3: "Because signals are stronger on VHF and UHF frequencies": Signals are not inherently stronger on VHF/UHF in every local situation; the operating principle is spectrum courtesy.
